scenarios.context: Two students want to improve recycling at their school.

speakerA.en: Look at all this rubbish in the yard. Why is nobody using the bins?
We should start a recycling project. What do you think?
And we can make posters to explain it to the younger students.
I'll write a short plan today. Could you help me draw the posters?

speakerB.en: There are no separate bins for plastic or paper. Everything goes in one bin.
I agree. We could put out three coloured bins for paper, plastic and glass.
Let's ask the principal for permission. I'm sure she'll support us.
Of course. I'm good at drawing. We can start next week.

scenarios.context: Two friends talk about air pollution and climate change.

speakerA.en: The air was terrible today. I could hardly see the mountains.
Is it also connected to climate change? The summers are hotter now.
That's scary. What can ordinary people do?
I'll ask my parents to take the bus sometimes. Small actions matter.

speakerB.en: It's because of pollution from cars and factories. It's getting worse every year.
Yes, scientists say the Earth is getting warmer because of too much carbon in the air.
We can use public transport, walk or cycle more, and save electricity.
Exactly. If everyone does a little, the result can be big.

scenarios.context: A girl invites her friend to a community clean-up.

speakerA.en: Our neighbourhood is organising a clean-up day on Saturday. Do you want to join?
We'll collect rubbish in the park and along the river, and plant some trees.
It starts at nine. Bring gloves, water and a hat. The community centre will give us bags.
Yes, children are welcome if an adult comes with them. Your mum can join us, too.

speakerB.en: That sounds interesting. What will we do?
What time does it start? Do we need to bring anything?
Great. Can I bring my younger brother? He loves nature.
Perfect. I'm excited. It's a good opportunity to meet new people.

scenarios.context: A student asks her friend about a festival in her culture.

speakerA.en: Is there a special festival in your country, Leila? I'd love to learn about it.
How do people celebrate it?
That's a beautiful tradition. Do you have special food, too?
I'd like to experience it someday.

speakerB.en: Yes, Nowruz, the Persian New Year. It begins on the first day of spring.
We clean our houses, visit our relatives and set a special table with seven items.
Yes, we eat rice with herbs and fish. Children usually get small gifts from the elders.
You're welcome to visit us. My family would be delighted to have you.

scenarios.context: Two friends decide to help someone in their community.

speakerA.en: Have you seen Mr. Rahimi lately? He hasn't come out for a week.
His leg hurt last week, so he can't go shopping. We should help him.
What else could we do? I don't want him to feel lonely.
I'll write him a card and bring some fruit.

speakerB.en: No, I haven't. He's elderly and lives alone. Maybe he needs help.
Good idea. Let's ask our parents first, and then knock on his door.
We can visit him after school, chat over tea, or read the newspaper to him.
He'll be so happy. A strong community looks after all its members.
